verdict.rationale: LangSmith documents grouping into threads ("Inspect threads and runs in the Messages, Turns, and Details views") and agent-run tracing via SDKs, decorators and OpenTelemetry. Hands-on community evidence confirms step-by-step traces through agent graphs with per-step inputs and outputs. One commenter says it "only shows the LLM inferences" outside LangChain, but this is a vague integration complaint and is not treated as a concrete counter-example. missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of the nested span/run-tree hierarchy, documented details on how runs are assigned to sessions/threads, independent corroboration for non-LangChain stacks.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace multi-step agent runs as nested spans grouped into sessions or threads

citations.quote: Inspect threads and runs in the Messages, Turns, and Details views.
Traces are the record of what your agents did in production.
The power of LangSmith is seeing full traces moving through the graph and being able to inspect the inputs and outputs for each step
Unify traces when calling your deployed Agent Server from another service using RemoteGraph or the SDK.
